title: SDK Bootcamp Labs — Curated Playlist and Problem Sets
content:
Purpose and audience:
This document is a compact, instructor-friendly playlist of hands-on labs and short problem sets designed to run as a 2-day or 5-day SDK bootcamp for new hires, advocates, or partner engineers. Audience: backend/frontend engineers, platform integrators, and solutions engineers who will embed Redwood SDKs into production apps. Goal: compress first 2–4 weeks of high-signal learning into focused, timeboxed exercises that teach API ergonomics, failure modes, telemetry, and production-ready patterns.

Design principles (why this is different):
- Low friction: each lab runs in 15–45 minutes and uses the same starter repo to avoid environment setup overhead.
- Incremental mental model: exercises progress from happy-path usage to resilience, to cost/perf knobs (batching, caching, quantization profiles).
- Telemetry-first: every lab includes explicit telemetry checks (what events to expect, debug queries, how to surface in Console).
- Teach rollouts and fallbacks: simulate model variant rollouts and routing policies so teams learn safe deploy patterns.
- Reproducible evaluation: each problem set has an acceptance checklist and a minimal test script.

High-level schedule options:
- 2-day sprint (compact): Day 1: Labs 1–4 (core SDK, auth, streaming, error handling). Day 2: Labs 5–8 (batching, caching, telemetry, rollout simulation).
- 5-day extended (recommended for deeper practice): Day 1: env + core patterns; Day 2: telemetry & tests; Day 3: performance & batching; Day 4: private/dedicated integration; Day 5: capstone (integrate an example app + run smoke tests).

Starter repo and prerequisites:
- Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-bootcamp-starter (branch: bootcamp-ready)
- Node >= 18 or Python 3.10
- Local CLI token (redwood-cli) configured with a test sandbox key
- Docker for local caching proxy lab (optional)
- Estimated total install time: 10–15 minutes

Lab 1 — Hello SDK (15 min)
Objective: initialize the SDK, make a single generation, inspect headers and latency.
Steps (timeboxed):
1. Clone starter repo + npm/pip install (5 min).
2. Set REDWOOD_API_KEY and run example: node examples/hello.js or python examples/hello.py (5 min).
3. Inspect response envelope: model name, token counts, request_id. (5 min)
Acceptance: example returns 200, request_id appears, minimal latency logged in console.
Telemetry check: Console should show a request span for /v1/generate and the token_count metric appears in traces.

Lab 2 — Streaming and partial output handling (30 min)
Objective: wire streaming handlers, implement UI-friendly partial render with truncation/backpressure handling.
Key teaching points: SSE vs chunked HTTP vs Websocket; how to resume/abort; memory safety (KV cache size).
Problem set: Implement a minimal streaming component that cancels after 5s and verifies partial_text length <= 120 chars.
Acceptance: component renders partial text progressively and cancels cleanly without orphaned inflight requests.
Linked telemetry: remove-streaming event, aborted_request boolean in logs.

Lab 3 — Retry, timeouts, and graceful degradation (30 min)
Objective: simulate transient infra failures; implement exponential backoff, circuit breaker, and model-fallback.
Scenario: the hosted endpoint returns 503 for 2/5 calls. Configure SDK wrapper with 3 retries and fallback to a smaller model.
Acceptance: client returns a response when fallback is triggered; metrics show increase in fallback_count and retry attempts.

Lab 4 — Batching and cost-per-token visibility (45 min)
Objective: implement a batching layer for small requests (chat completions) and measure unit cost improvements.
Exercises:
- Use starter batching helper to create a batch window (20ms) and batch size 8.
- Measure per-token cost with and without batching using the provided cost-runner script.
Acceptance: batching reduces cost-per-1000-tokens by measurable delta on the provided synthetic traces.
Telemetry: token_batch_size histogram, batching_latency P90.

Lab 5 — KV/prefix caching lab (30 min)
Objective: add prefix caching for repeated prompts (e.g., assistant system messages) and evaluate cache hit ratio.
Problem set: instrument a cache with TTL=5m and simulate 1000 requests with 60% identical prefixes.
Acceptance: cache_hit_ratio >= 0.6 and P95 latency drops by expected percentage.

Lab 6 — Private/Dedicated quicktest (optional, 45 min)
Objective: walk the team through connecting the SDK to a Dedicated pool or Private deployment (VPC test).
Checklist: verify TLS, KMS integration (test key), and restricted egress rules in the sample env.
Acceptance: request flows through dedicated endpoint and Console marks it as "dedicated-route" in tracing metadata.

Lab 7 — Rollouts, canaries, and A/B routing (45 min)
Objective: construct a canary rollout using SDK routing hints and test automatic fallback.
Exercises: define two model variants (m-small, m-large), route 5% traffic to m-large, then simulate latency spike and validate automatic fallback kicks in.
Acceptance: rollout metrics reflect weight and fallback events; sample client experiences <1% error rate during spike.

Lab 8 — Observability root-cause (45 min)
Objective: use the Console and exported traces to find the root cause of a simulated quality regression introduced by a prompt change.
Tasks: run evaluation harness on 50 golden prompts, compare model outputs, open a regression ticket template (prefilled).
Acceptance: identify a prompt cluster with regression score at least 15% worse and attach minimal repro case to ticket.

Capstone (extended): Build a tiny bug-tracker assistant
- Combine streaming UI, caching, batching, and telemetry hooks into a mini app.
- Walkthrough includes a CI smoke test script that runs the evaluation harness and fails the PR if quality drops >5%.

Evaluation and scoring rubric:
- Smoke tests pass (functional): yes/no
- Resilience (retries + fallback): logs show <=1 uncaught error per 1000 requests
- Telemetry coverage: traces, latency histograms, and token metrics present
- Acceptance: each team should be able to complete the 2-day sprint with the starter repo and produce the capstone within one week post-bootcamp.

Facilitator notes and traps:
- Avoid long environment setup; pre-provision demo tokens and a sandbox dedicated endpoint.
- Emphasize small wins: show Console telemetry within 2–3 minutes after first request.
- Common confusion: distinguishing SDK retry (client-side) from server-side retries—include a short visual in the intro slide deck.

Unresolved questions (to decide in next sprint):
- Do we want a slim containerized lab that runs fully offline for vendor events? (pros/cons)
- Standardize the exact telemetry event names across languages (node/python/ts) for search and dashboards.
- Should the bootcamp include an optional security module on KMS/HSM hands-on?

Appendix — Quick commands and snippets:
- Clone and start (Node):
  git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-bootcamp-starter.git
  cd sdk-bootcamp-starter && npm ci
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sandbox_live_xxx
  node examples/hello.js
- Run batch cost runner (Python):
  pip install -r requirements.txt
  python tools/cost_runner.py --iterations 200 --batching on
- Run telemetry smoke test (shell):
  ./tools/telemetry_smoke.sh --expected-metrics request_count,token_count,traces

If this looks good I’ll:
- convert to a lightweight slide deck (15 slides) for facilitators
- create the Capstone rubric as a checklist JSON in the starter repo
- prototype the offline container next sprint (ENG-xxxx)
